St. Simon the Zealot

Saints

St. Simon the Zealot

St. Simon the Canaanite · St. Simon Zelotes

Period
First century
Region
Eastern Mediterranean
Titles / vocation
Apostle · Martyr
Commemoration
May 10

Introduction

St. Simon is one of the Twelve; the OCA life preserves the tradition of his missionary journeys and crucifixion.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomWritings and legacyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Crucified, according to the published tradition.

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The published tradition connects him with Cana and identifies him as the bridegroom at the wedding. John’s Gospel does not name that bridegroom.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 1; Published biographical account,paragraph 2; Published biographical account,paragraph 3 · [2] Public-domain Bible translation · John 2:1–11 (KJV)

And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.

Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;

Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;

Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.

These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not:

But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.

And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand.

Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Matthew 10: 1–8

Life and notable events

The life describes his participation in Pentecost and preaching from Britain toward the Black Sea. These extended itineraries belong to later tradition.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 2; Published biographical account,paragraph 4

And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:

And both Jesus was called, and his disciples, to the marriage.

And when they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus saith unto him, They have no wine.

Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.

His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.

And there were set there six waterpots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece.

Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.

And he saith unto them, Draw out now, and bear unto the governor of the feast. And they bare it.

When the ruler of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and knew not whence it was: (but the servants which drew the water knew;) the governor of the feast called the bridegroom,

And saith unto him, Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept the good wine until now.

This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

The Cana narrative; the Gospel leaves the bridegroom unnamed. The identification with Simon comes from the separately cited later tradition.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · John 2: 1–11

Then returned they unto Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is from Jerusalem a sabbath day’s journey.

And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.

These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Acts 1: 12–14

Death and martyrdom

The OCA account says he suffered martyrdom by crucifixion; it does not establish a precise execution year.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 2

Writings and legacy

The account distinguishes this St. Simon from St. Simon Peter and from the Lord’s relative who became bishop of Jerusalem.

[1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 3

And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.

And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.

And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.

And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

The apostolic Pentecost narrative, not an individual death account.

[2] Public-domain Bible translation · Acts 2: 1–4

Chronology

  1. Ministry of Christ

    Named among the Twelve.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 2

  2. Pentecost

    Receives the Spirit with the apostles.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 2

  3. Later mission

    Tradition describes preaching and crucifixion.

    [1] Official Orthodox hagiographic account · Published biographical account,paragraph 2; Published biographical account,paragraph 4
